fullAnalysis: Puzzle #675 offers five clues — Warning, Street, Vital, Peace, and Equal — that seem to span safety, geography, medicine, culture, and mathematics. The surface categories appear unrelated, which creates a momentary sense of difficulty. But the shared connector is hiding in plain sight: every clue forms a well-known phrase when you place the word 'sign' after it.

Warning sign and street sign are so common they barely need testing. Peace sign and equal sign are fixed cultural and mathematical terms. Vital signs, the one plural form in the set, refers to the standard medical measurements of pulse, blood pressure, and temperature. All five phrases are in active daily use across completely different domains, which is exactly what makes this category clean despite the wide variety of clues.
solutionNarrative: I started with the two most obvious phrases: warning sign and street sign. Both landed immediately and I had a working hypothesis within seconds. From there I tested the remaining three against 'sign' in sequence — peace sign, equal sign, vital signs — and each one produced a phrase I already knew. No false starts, no backtracking.

The only moment of hesitation came with Vital, because vital signs is plural while the others use the singular form. I almost dismissed it, then reminded myself that the conventional phrase is vital signs, not vital sign. That was enough. Once all five clues checked out, I stopped second-guessing and committed to the answer.

lessons.title: Start with the most obvious phrase and test outward
lessons.body: Warning sign and street sign are so familiar that they almost solve themselves. Once two clues confirm a connector, apply it to the remaining three before considering any other hypothesis. Common phrases are usually the right path.

lessons.title: Different domains can share one clean connector
lessons.body: Street comes from geography, vital from medicine, peace from culture, equal from mathematics — yet 'sign' works for all five. A connector does not need every clue to come from the same field. Focus on the shared word, not the shared topic.

lessons.title: Plural forms are still valid
lessons.body: Vital signs uses the plural while the other clues pair with a singular sign. Pinpoint accepts this variation as long as the compound phrase is a recognised term in standard usage. Do not discard a good hypothesis just because one clue takes a slightly different grammatical form.
